source.title: FALCON: Fine-grained Activation Manipulation by Contrastive Orthogonal Unalignment for Large Language Model
source.authors: Jinwei Hu; Zhenglin Huang; Xiangyu Yin; Wenjie Ruan; Guangliang Cheng; Yi Dong; Xiao-Wei Huang

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or corruption. The text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own unlearning and recovery-attack results for FALCON and argues that this method resists recovery, refining the broader claim that unlearned knowledge is readily recoverable.
record.gate_note: The paper tests FALCON's unlearning and recovery resistance. It reports WMDP, MMLU and perplexity results, enhanced GCG recovery scores, a logit-lens probe, and a qualitative comparison of recovery vulnerability after omitting components. It does not report tests of recovery by fine-tuning, quantization, prompt rephrasing alone, or activation-direction ablation. The MI layer-selection values and computational-efficiency results do not test the claim's recovery predictions.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes FALCON, a new unlearning method, and runs its own recovery attacks against it on Yi-6B-Chat: enhanced GCG jailbreak prefixes (QA and chat templates), logit-lens probing, and an RMU comparison. It argues the knowledge is removed, not masked. This bears on F, and also on A, C and E. The record wrongly marks E as untested: enhanced GCG is a jailbreak, a prompting-only attack with no weight change.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors also claim FALCON resists recovery better than RMU (Table 12). They attribute this to fundamental representational change rather than superficial masking.
record.recipe_differences: FALCON is a new representation-guided unlearning method using MI-guided parameter selection, contrastive representation unlearning, principal offset vectors and gradient projection. The paper does not reproduce the original gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU recovery attack recipes as its own method.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery results are reported for WMDP-Bio versus WMDP-Cyber, multiple GCG iteration counts, and with versus without chat templates. The paper also reports greater jailbreaking vulnerability when gradient projection or POVs are omitted.
record.problems: Recovery experiments are mainly on Yi-6B-Chat. The paper does not report a never-trained model comparison for recovery attacks or an explicit chance-level reference for WMDP. Logit-lens values are shown only in a figure without stated numerical values. Some attack comparisons and component-ablation vulnerability findings are qualitative or lack a stated attack configuration.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant numeric results were omitted. The paper's MUSE and TOFU unlearning-quality results, MI layer-selection results, and runtime analyses do not test the recovery attacks specified in the claim.

untested.parts: Recovery by fine-tuning, quantization or direction ablation. Recovery attacks on Zephyr and Mistral.
Entire version: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Activation-direction ablation is not run; only logit-lens probing is reported.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information; only GCG jailbreak prefixes are tested.
Resistance to fine-tuning relearning, quantization and direction ablation. Recovery on models other than Yi-6B-Chat.

missing.what: RMU and other baseline WMDP/MMLU scores, useful as comparators for A (e.g. RMU on Yi reaches only 50.8 Bio while keeping MMLU above 60)

record.verdict_notes: Recovery tests cover only Yi-6B-Chat and only jailbreak/probe attacks; there is no relearning, quantization or direction ablation, the strongest known attacks for B to D. Appendix D.2.5 says resistance experiments used per-sample updates on the forget set, a configuration that may differ from the main-table runs. The Table 12 attack is unspecified beyond 'identical recovery settings'. The RMU comparator was tuned to keep MMLU above 60, which left it weakly unlearned on Yi (50.8). The ablation vulnerability claims (r34, r35) carry no numbers, so they are given no label.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not state a chance-level reference for WMDP, and it does not compare recovery with a model that never saw the target knowledge. Recovery is evaluated on Yi-6B-Chat, not across all tested models.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples is reported.
No activation-direction ablation is reported. The logit-lens probe does not establish whether inaccessible knowledge was deleted or merely blocked.
No quantization of unlearned weights is reported.

No prompt rephrasing, other-language, or in-context-information recovery test is reported. Enhanced GCG prefix attacks are reported, but do not test prompting-only recovery as specified in this version.

Resistance is evaluated with logit-lens probing and enhanced GCG attacks, including chat templates. Fine-tuning, quantization, activation-direction ablation, and prompting-only recovery are not tested.

relation.reason: The paper runs its own recovery attacks (enhanced GCG, logit lens) and an RMU comparison.

tranche.reason: The study's own results (Tables 4 and 11, Fig. 4) show no recovery for FALCON, so E and C do not hold for this method. It argues explicitly for 'fundamental changes... rather than superficial knowledge masking'. That fits T5 and matches the record's challenges labels on C and E.

source_check.notes: All attacks are the authors' own, on Yi-6B-Chat only, with no controls. Table 11 is readable once the stray page number '23' is dropped: chat-template Bio 26.7/25.9/27.6/27.6, Cyber 27.2/27.3/25.2/28.1. The statements' ranges 27.6-28.9 and 24.7-26.4 are QA format (Table 4) only. Table 12's RMU attack is given only as 'identical recovery settings'.

statements.correction: 2502.01472: enhanced GCG (gradient-optimized jailbreak prefixes after Łucki et al.; white-box gradient access, weights not modified), Yi-6B-Chat, QA format (Table 4): Bio 27.6-28.9 (unlearned 27.7, original 65.4); Cyber 24.7-26.4 (unlearned 25.3, original 42.6).
statements.problem: The FALCON numbers are right (Table 4, QA format), but the shared condition 'with no weight access' is wrong for this study. Enhanced GCG is gradient-based prefix optimization and needs white-box access; it only leaves the weights unchanged. The synthesis itself calls Enhanced GCG white-box in E.support[0].

statements.correction: 2502.01472 Table 12 (Yi-6B-Chat; attack described only as 'identical recovery settings'; the study's attack in Sec. 5.3 is enhanced GCG): RMU Bio 50.8->58.5 ± 3.2 (original 65.4); RMU Cyber 33.5->41.8 ± 2.1 (original 42.6); FALCON Bio 27.7->28.1 ± 0.5, Cyber 25.3->25.5 ± 0.8. Either add this to the statement and its conditions, or drop the citation.
statements.problem: The statement cites r30 and r32 but never describes them. Its conditions limit it to Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B and say WMDP-Cyber moves little. Yet cited row r32 shows RMU on Yi-6B-Chat Cyber regaining nearly all removed accuracy. The only part about this study that is right is that FALCON moves little.

statements.correction: 2502.01472 r13: FALCON on Yi-6B-Chat, logit lens on MLP, attention and residual components. Figure only: the text says scores stay near the unlearned baseline, far below the original. Add this to the statement or drop the citation (it is already used in C.against[0]).
statements.problem: The statement says nothing about FALCON but cites r13 (Yi-6B-Chat logit lens, figure-only). The citation does not match the text.
